title: Connections between the proof branches
scope: These connections use the original valued field, actual classical or completed Borel objects as specified, ordinary domains, allowed symmetric middle-positive separately closed backgrounds, and the full original test classes. A proof input identifies an ingredient of the cited argument; it does not assert that one displayed input alone is sufficient. The existing mathematical edition and source statuses are unchanged.

nodes.title: Available degree-one action and full Leibniz rule
nodes.summary: Use the established R6 input: every actual delta-form of total bidegree (1,1) acts on every allowed background S of degree p<n, intrinsically on all original tests. Its agreement with PS multiplication and the full PS Leibniz rule give M_S(d′β)=d′(β∧S) and M_S(d″γ)=d″(γ∧S). This is an available input, not an additional open conjecture or a higher-degree arbitrary-current product.

QA1–QA7: the input and full derivative compatibility

hypotheses: Fix a strict original Laurent domain V and one allowed background S extending to a neighborhood of its closure; the remaining degree is q=n−p≥1.

Use the analytic Laurent-collar and affinoid capacity-localization results, the original coefficient controls and countably cofinal compact test stages, with the full classical normalized tester family on the stated domain.

The actual negative classical power classes have compact strict negative sublevel closures, canonical no loss and the displayed finite power energy where those conditions are required. Local coefficient finiteness is required when first defining the nonpolar product.

For the completed bounded calculus use actual Borel limits in ordinary-open outer capacity. Keep the coefficient budget a+b≤q+σ and distinguish closed locally finite limits from individual restricted truncation stages.
relations.explanation: The bounded weighted recursion, relative coefficient estimates, quasicontinuity and boundary comparison supply the local multiplier and sublevel estimates. The analytic collar and capacity-localization arguments put them on the required Laurent domain. These inputs support the no-loss criterion, capacity-energy equivalence, graded tail bounds and bounded Borel completion used in the energy branch. The proof uses outer capacity and does not require general relative raw/outer equality on arbitrary Borel sets.

hypotheses: Work on one original ordinary domain with a symmetric middle-positive separately closed background Q of degree (p,p), where p<n.
Each scalar difference f=a−b has actual locally bounded classical psh summands; use finitely many such presentations on every compact test support.

Retain finite polarization, original coefficient-Radon control, and the smooth convex decomposition of scalar functions on an interval containing the local range. All multipliers use the actual Borel values.
relations.explanation: Simultaneous bounded regularizations and the weighted theorem pass the three-term energy identity to actual differences. Positivity gives coefficient-Radon control, and polarization treats cross terms. A finite difference of convex coordinatewise-increasing compositions passes every weighted term of the smooth chain identities. The resulting scalar calculus is intrinsic and needs no general analytic relation-descent conjecture.

links.label: LC1–LC2: smooth scalar calculus and proof from the bounded input

hypotheses: Use a finite real quadratic presentation P=Σcν[hν][kν], with constant cν∈R, whose continuous PL/PS scalars are admissible on one ordinary representative over the original field; retain the full actual delta curvatures and closed-cell face data.

The quadratic action uses an allowed original S of degree 0≤p≤n−2. The separately established degree-one action and full derivative compatibility are explicit joint inputs; no higher-degree arbitrary-current multiplication is assumed.

Retain α_P=A₀−Z_P with the complete singular term A₀=½D_δ(Σcνhνkν), all original compact smooth complementary tests and every actual refinement. When P is an actual zero, its transgression class lies in the actual Aeppli quotient.
relations.explanation: Bounded products define the finite signed quadratic action, while the degree-one operation identifies the action of each scalar-curvature primitive. Full derivative compatibility and the intrinsic Leibniz identity give A_S(P)=D M_S(α_P)=−D M_S(Z_P). This is the bridge to the quadratic certificate arguments; it does not construct an exact certificate for every actual zero.

hypotheses: Specify Green currents g_Z satisfying Dg_Z+δ_Z=ω_Z, their permitted cycle classes and an actual first-energy truncation class on the intended ordinary domains.

General actual-relation descent is itself still open. In a curvature-generated expression it would make the differential presentation intrinsic; it would not define multiplication by a cycle current on its own.
Still prove proper-intersection or replacement hypotheses, coefficient integrability, and independence of admissible presentations and truncations, with all relevant degree and boundary conditions.
Still establish the required mapping properties, Green symmetry and comparison with existing smooth, formal and delta-form products on their common domains.
relations.explanation: The two branches have different roles in the proposed construction: relation descent addresses algebraic presentation independence, while capacity tails and mixed energy control limiting integrals. They meet at the Green-product problem, but cycle multiplication, intersection, integrability and comparison remain additional mathematical interfaces. This connection is a research route, not an established implication to finite-energy intersection theory.
